medications.purpose: Lower blood pressure to target <140/90 mmHg
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 first_line_treatment: ACE inhibitor for patients <55 years and not Afro‑Caribbean

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥60 mL/min/1.73m²; baseline renal function and potassium must be checked before starting ACE‑I and repeated 1–2 weeks after dose change (NICE NG136 monitoring).
Serum potassium not provided – assume normal; must be measured before ACE‑I initiation and after dose adjustments.

Pregnancy status not documented – patient is of reproductive age; ensure effective contraception (already on norethindrone) and counsel that ACE‑I must be stopped if pregnancy occurs (NICE contraindicated ACE‑I in pregnancy).
QRISK cardiovascular risk score not calculated – required by NICE for overall risk assessment and statin consideration.
BMI not recorded – needed for lifestyle advice and dose considerations for future diuretics.
Baseline fasting glucose/HbA1c already 6.4% (prediabetes) – monitor glucose while on ACE‑I.
No ambulatory blood pressure monitoring data – clinic BP used for decision; consider ambulatory monitoring if available.
treatment_summary: Start ramipril 2.5 mg daily as first‑line ACE‑inhibitor therapy for essential hypertension per NICE NG136. Obtain baseline renal function, electrolytes, and confirm effective contraception before initiation. Review BP in 4 weeks and titrate up to 5 mg daily if target not reached, with ongoing monitoring of renal function and potassium.
